title: Decoding adverse childhood experiences: Molecular, psychosocial, digital, and neural characterization
summary: This study investigates how adverse childhood experiences, also referred to as childhood trauma, affect the mental health of young people. It is already known that such experiences increase the risk of mental health disorders in adulthood and can make treatment more difficult. However, a deeper understanding of the exact biological and psychological mechanisms involved is still lacking. The aim of this project is to gain a more comprehensive understanding of these relationships. To this end, various factors are being analyzed simultaneously in a study involving young adults aged 16 to 30. We are investigating not only clinical symptoms, but also (1) psychosocial characteristics (i.e., clinical questionnaires), (2) digital markers (clinical interviews and MRI scans), and (3) biological markers (biospecimens).
conditions: Problems related to negative life events in childhood

interventions.name: Case group: Participants with childhood trauma who are diagnosed with a mental disorder will undergo a clinical interview, complete online questionnaires, and provide biosamples at the baseline visit.
Healthy control group: Participants in the healthy control group will undergo a clinical interview, complete online questionnaires, and provide biosamples at the baseline visit.

All participants: All participants enrolled at the baseline visit, including both the case and healthy control groups, will complete online questionnaires 6 and 12 months after the baseline visit. The total observation period is 12 months.

Case-group follow-up subgroup: A selected subgroup of 60 participants from the case group will be invited to take part in an extended follow-up phase of the study. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For all groups (patient and control): 
- Fluency in German

Inlusion criteria for the patient group: 
- The diagnosis of a mental disorder was made by the treating physician and is confirmed using the Diagnostic Interview for Mental Disorders in Adults (DIPS-OA) or the Diagnostic Interview for Mental Disorders in Children and Adolescents (Kinder-DIPS-OA), according to DSM-5 and ICD-10 criteria.

Inclusion criteria for the control group: 
- No confirmed diagnosis of a mental disorder, as assessed using the Diagnostic Interview for Mental Disorders in Adults (DIPS-OA) or the Diagnostic Interview for Mental Disorders in Children and Adolescents (Kinder-DIPS-OA), according to DSM-5 and ICD-10 criteria.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for all groups: 
- Previously participated in studies conducted at the Department of Psychiatry, University Hospital Jena
- Psychotic disorders identified using the DIPS-OA or Kinder-DIPS-OA
- Neurodevelopmental disorders (e.g., autism spectrum disorders)
- Severe disorder due to illicit substance or alcohol use within the past 6 months, as identified using the DIPS-OA or Kinder-DIPS-OA
- Unstable or severe endocrine, cardiovascular, or neurological disorders (e.g., stroke, type 1 diabetes)
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding

A subgroup of participants will be included in the MRI examinations and longitudinal biosample collection. Additional exclusion criteria apply to this subgroup.
Additional exclusion criteria for the MRI group: 
- Contraindications to MRI (e.g., pacemakers, hearing aids, neurostimulation devices, insulin pumps, other potentially ferromagnetic implants, etc.)
